source.snippet: So much for buying another OVH based VPS in Singapore/Asia for some of my friends to use when they are 100% out of stock and/or other good hosting providers have doubled their pricing in the last few months.... God, I love AI.... and hate it.... Yet growing my web projects and everything is too pricey right now. My small 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM, and 75GB NVME VPS at $10 is the best I am gonna do unless something changes... (10 points, 9 comments)

problem_statement: AI infrastructure demand is driving up VPS prices and causing stock shortages, making affordable cloud hosting unavailable for small web developers and indie builders who previously relied on sub-$15/mo VPS plans in Asia-Pacific regions.
target_segment: Solo developers, indie hackers, and small-team web project operators who rely on budget VPS hosting (~$5–$20/mo range) for personal and commercial projects.
notes: Buyer signal present: commenter is actively spending on VPS ($10/mo current plan, wants more capacity). The broader thread (9 comments, 10 points) suggests shared frustration. Market gap: a service that aggregates or arbitrages remaining affordable VPS inventory, or a coop/reseller model, could capture this segment. Willingness to pay is established (already paying, wants to pay more for more capacity).
